summary_ja: 派生商品取引の与信相当額をSA-CCR又は期待エクスポージャー方式で算出し（五営業日以内の為替取引は除外可）、長期決済期間取引への準用、レポ取引への期待エクスポージャー方式の適用、クレジット・デリバティブの算出不要の場合、会計上のCVAの控除を定める。
summary_en: Derivative credit equivalents are calculated with SA-CCR or the expected exposure method (FX contracts of up to 5 business days may be excluded); the same applies to long settlement transactions; credit derivatives used as protection are exempt; accounting CVA is deducted per netting set.

sections_en.第四節: Derivative Transactions and Long Settlement Period Transactions

paragraphs: The credit equivalent amounts of forwards, swaps, options and other derivative transactions shall be calculated using SA-CCR or the expected exposure method as provided in the following Article through Article 54; provided, however, that foreign exchange-related transactions with an original maturity of five business days or less may be excluded from the calculation of credit equivalent amounts.

The provisions of the preceding paragraph shall apply mutatis mutandis to the calculation of the credit equivalent amounts of long settlement period transactions (meaning transactions for the delivery or settlement of securities, etc. and their consideration (excluding those falling under derivative transactions) for which it has been agreed that the period from the trade date to the due date of delivery or settlement will exceed five business days or the period under market practice, and which, where they fall under the transactions listed in the following items, satisfy the requirement specified in that item; the same applies hereinafter). In this case, an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach may use different methods for derivative transactions and long settlement period transactions. (i) Delivery-versus-payment transactions (meaning transactions in which securities, etc. and funds are settled simultaneously (excluding those relating to repo-style transactions); the same applies hereinafter): transactions before the contractual settlement date, and transactions for which the number of business days on which payment or delivery has not been made after the contractual settlement date has passed (hereinafter referred to as the "number of business days elapsed") is four days or less. (ii) Of non-delivery-versus-payment transactions (meaning transactions in which securities, etc. and funds are not settled simultaneously (excluding those relating to repo-style transactions); the same applies hereinafter), those in which the delivery of securities, etc. or payment of funds to the counterparty is made before the counter-transaction: transactions in which the delivery of securities, etc. or payment of funds to the counterparty has not been made.

Where an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach uses the expected exposure method as provided in Article 49 through Article 54, it may also calculate the credit equivalent amounts of repo-style transactions and margin lending and similar overseas transactions using the expected exposure method.

In the cases listed in the following items, an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach is not required to calculate the credit equivalent amount of credit derivatives under the provisions of this Article through Article 54. (i) Where the credit derivative is used as a credit risk mitigation technique for an exposure held by the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach (excluding those subject to the calculation of market risk equivalent amounts). (ii) Where the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach, as the protection provider of a credit derivative, applies the provisions of item (vi) of the table of paragraph (1) of the preceding Article, Article 112, Article 114 or Article 115.

In calculating credit equivalent amounts in this Section, an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach shall deduct the amount of CVA recognized in financial accounting from the credit equivalent amount calculated for each netting set (meaning, for transactions under a legally effective bilateral netting contract, the set of those transactions, and for other transactions, each individual transaction; the same applies hereinafter); provided, however, that where the result is below zero, it shall be zero.
